structured_output.justification: The shipment record shows 260 kg billed weight and 800 km distance, placing this consignment in the §1 'up to and including 500 kg' band at ₹18.00/km, yielding base freight of 14400. The express service premium of 15% (§2) correctly applies given service_level is 'express', adding 2160 on the base. The fuel surcharge of 12% (§3) then applies to the combined base-plus-express figure, per its stated compounding basis. No special_handling values are present on the shipment record, so the §4 residential accessorial (whitelisted as the only payable accessorial under §5) does not fire, and no other accessorial is contractually payable. Recomputing the trace step by step against the verbatim contract text confirms the expected amount is correctly derived and the billed amount includes an unexplained excess with no clause supporting it.

memo_narrative.what_happened: Falcon billed consignment FF-8005 (260 kg, Mumbai–Bengaluru, 800 km, express) at a figure above what the base freight, express premium, and fuel surcharge calculation under the contract supports.
memo_narrative.why: Applying the §1 weight-band rate, the §2 express premium, and the §3 fuel surcharge in sequence to the shipment's actual weight and distance produces a lower figure than billed, and no accessorial under §4/§5 applies since no residential handling is flagged, so the excess above the amount above is not supported by any clause.
memo_narrative.recommended_action: Raise a billing dispute with Falcon Freight within the §7 45-day window, citing §1–§3 and §5, and request a corrected invoice for consignment FF-8005.
